name: Fidel Velázquez Sánchez
summary:
Fidel Velázquez Sánchez was the preeminent Mexican union leader of the 20th century. In 1936 he was one of the original founders, along with Vicente Lombardo Toledano, of the Confederation of Mexican Workers (CTM), the national labor federation most closely associated with the ruling party, the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI). He replaced Lombardo as the leader of the CTM in 1941, then expelled him from it in 1948.

He led the CTM, which grew increasingly corrupt and conservative, until his death in 1997. Fidel Velázquez Sánchez was a labor organizers from Nicolás Romero (1900-05-12, Nicolás Romero–1997-06-21). A moderately significant entity in the historical record. Relevant to economic history.

He played a key role in the CTM's growth and influence during his nearly six-decade tenure.
